tech.title: Anthropic S-1 Shows Red-Hot Growth, Risks, and Massive Computing Costs

It also lays out a long list of risk factors that include uncertainty over how the company plans to prevent its AI models from causing harm and protect itself from those liabilities. Anthropic is generating breakneck revenue growth, but it faces challenges such as uncertain access to compute. It has signaled that it could potentially spend $750 billion in the next few years on obtaining more compute capacity.

tech.title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
tech.summary: Anthropic asked an internal research model to design mini binders, small proteins that attach tightly to a target, against scorpion neurotoxins as part of its work in experimenting with how Claude can accelerate drug discovery. 17 of the 211 designs tested met Anthropic's criteria. Anthropic has not confirmed whether these binders neutralize scorpion venom in a cellular environment, so it is not claiming to have produced an antivenom. However, the study is a promising first step towards using AI to design credible binders against hard-to-target toxins in days, with lab confirmation within weeks. The challenge, as always, will be turning those binders into safe, affordable, and widely accessible drugs.

Practiced over time, workers will find themselves answering questions they used to ask, making decisions they used to need help with, and taking on problems they wouldn't have known how to approach.

tech.title: How To Use Decision Models for Evals
tech.summary: Decision models are an appealing alternative to LLM judges for automated evals. However, whether they're the right choice depends on the cost, performance, and latency requirements of the use case. Many people leave the default decision threshold at 0.50 without checking whether that's appropriate for the task, leaving a lot of performance on the table. This post shows how to tune thresholds to get the best results from decision models, compares cost and performance between models, and explores how to interpret model scores and how calibration can make them more useful.

It runs vLLM, SGLang, and more across clusters, turning single-node engines into production-grade serving on local hardware. llm-d provides tested deployment recipes for common production patterns that are adaptable starting points across models, hardware, and workloads. It runs production LLM inference across GPUs, TPUs, XPUs, CPUs, and emerging NPUs with consistent performance patterns, so teams can deploy once and scale anywhere with predictable cost and behavior.

It allows users to run Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code durably on Vercel or self-hosted on their own Postgres instance. durable-harness ensures that sessions survive crashes mid-turn and keep running even if the browser disconnects. Turns that lose function partway through continue from the log on a new one without manual retry and without repeating what already finished.

ai.title: Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform
ai.summary: Laminar is an in-house agent harness for Ramp's agentic products. It features secure conversation history storage, session compaction, standard interfaces for tool calling, message queuing and steering, subagents, multiplayer chat support, observability tooling, and much more. The first version of Laminar was built in six weeks with a small team of obsessive, experienced engineers who worked with and steered the agents. Its code was generated entirely by agents using the most powerful models available at the time. While building in-house has become cheaper, Ramp still needs good engineers to be on-call, keep the platform healthy, and figure out what product teams actually need and how it fits into the bigger picture.

webdev.title: Try the Postgres that took Clera from 100% CPU to 10–20%, with $300 in free credits
webdev.summary: Clera is an AI talent agent. Its Postgres database was stuck at 100% CPU for six straight days. Primary-key lookups took three seconds, and writes failed under load. So they tested Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale and ClickHouse Managed Postgres on their own production data. ClickHouse won. They then migrated 500+ tables overnight , and CPU now typically runs at 10–20%. Read how other teams are succeeding with ClickHouse Managed Postgres.

webdev.title: Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform
webdev.summary: Ramp consolidated its agentic products onto an in-house, model-agnostic harness built on Postgres, Temporal, and S3. Session state lives independently of disposable sandboxes, while asynchronous steering, subagents, and shared tracing support everything from support chat to long-running knowledge work. The first version took six weeks to build, with experienced engineers steering and reviewing agent-generated code.

webdev.title: On Alignment That Looks Wrong
webdev.summary: Flexbox can center an SVG perfectly while the drawing inside still looks misplaced. Inspecting the viewport, correcting uneven viewBox space, and adjusting visual weight at the asset or component level produces better results than scattering pixel nudges across consumers. Play buttons, circle sizing, and hanging punctuation show why mathematical alignment and optical balance differ.

webdev.title: How to Build a Decision Model Like Jev
webdev.summary: Decision models return probabilities over known outcomes in a single forward pass, avoiding the text generation and JSON parsing overhead of chat completions. This walkthrough starts with Hugging Face's /v1/systemone endpoint, then covers reserved option tokens, calibration, soft training targets, and tree batching for multiple questions over shared context.

webdev.title: The Future of CSS: My Top 10 Picks for Interop 2027
webdev.summary: Ten proposed Interop priorities include CSS functions, shaped borders, anchored container queries, visual reading order, and transitions to auto dimensions. Interactive examples show what each feature enables and where progressive enhancement can make it useful today. The case for staying current is practical: developers need enough CSS knowledge to guide coding agents beyond older patterns in their training data.

webdev.title: Gemini 4: Argon, Early Access Review
webdev.summary: Gemini 4 Argon handled an Android game, a UI redesign, and a distributed backend review well, with strong architectural planning and rapid changes across multiple files. Passing tests still hid cluttered layouts, accessibility regressions, and concurrency bugs, making browser checks, runtime logs, and adversarial self-review essential to getting reliable results.

webdev.title: Don't give your agent a token. Give it a proxy.
webdev.summary: What happens when you give your agent an access token and it gets hijacked? Relay (early access) keeps the credential at WorkOS and injects it only on requests to allowlisted hosts. A hijacked agent can still make bad calls, but it can't walk away with the token, and the session is a live process you can kill. Read the blog

webdev.title: TorchTPU
webdev.summary: TorchTPU provides a PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, with custom ATen kernels, an XLA compilation cache, and torch.compile integration. The repository includes distributed training support, debugging utilities, and examples for models including Llama, Qwen, and ResNet.

webdev.title: Voxtral 3
webdev.summary: Mistral's Voxtral 3 combines transcription, expressive speech generation, and a voice agent SDK for streaming conversations with tool calls. Transcription supports more than 50 languages, while speech synthesis covers more than 35 languages and 50 dialects. The models are available through an EU-hosted API or self-deployment.

webdev.title: Introducing tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust
webdev.summary: Cloudflare and VoidZero, in collaboration with the TypeScript team, are developing tsrs as a faithful Rust port of TypeScript within the Oxc toolchain. Early matched-configuration benchmarks report up to 8x faster checking and about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. An experimental npm release is available, though compatibility differences remain before a stable release.

webdev.title: Do web components have a future if nobody is writing them?
webdev.summary: Agentic coding challenges the case for web components as a way to make scarce, handwritten code reusable. Google's Modern Web Guidance offers little encouragement for new custom elements, and the argument extends to JavaScript frameworks as code generation becomes cheaper. Sandboxing and reuse remain possible defenses, but each has limitations.

Seven fixes merged in the first week, and a compaction change raised internal retention scores from 0.82 to 0.92. The reported gains come from internal experiments, and every accepted change still requires human code review.

webdev.title: From Use Case to GraphQL Operation: A Layered Approach for Agents
webdev.summary: A layered GraphQL approach lets agents start with local persisted operations, search an operation index, and reach for schema-driven query building or schema evolution only when needed. Persisting useful operations back into the index reduces repeated work, while fit evaluation determines when an existing query is sufficient and when the agent needs a more dynamic approach.

infosec.title: Block a simulated attack with FortiGate on AWS
infosec.summary: Traffic moving between your AWS Region and Outposts can bypass inspection if your security stack isn't positioned in the middle. This solution template deploys a fully configured FortiGate Next-Generation Firewall with AWS Gateway Load Balancer in one AWS CloudFormation stack. What you get: • Automated deployment: VPCs, Transit Gateway, IAM roles, and security policies — pre-configured. • Unified hybrid inspection: Monitor north-south and east-west traffic across VPCs and Outposts from one dashboard. • Hands-on IPS test: Create a sensor and block a simulated malicious download, step by step. Deploy the solution template →

infosec.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
infosec.summary: Researchers at Claroc found 6,800 Meta Muse share links through passive DNS searches. The links included conversation titles in their subdomains, making them searchable. Samples exposed executive-search notes, revenue reviews, loan applications, bank-fraud details, property records, and staff calendars. Meta paused the sharing feature on October 20 while reviewing the report.

infosec.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support 26.2.3 suffers auth bypass CVE-2026-102764
infosec.summary: BeyondTrust Remote Support versions 26.2.3 and earlier are affected by CVE-2026-102764, a critical authentication bypass and arbitrary file upload vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.3. CVE-2026-102764 lets unauthenticated attackers perform file operations, escalate to root, and access credential vaults. A suspected Chinese state-sponsored espionage group, Armory Castle (UNC5221), has actively exploited this zero-day flaw since late August to deploy custom webshells such as BARECLAW for persistence and lateral movement. BeyondTrust released security patches in October for self-hosted customers, prompting CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security to advise organizations to restrict external access to appliances and conduct forensic reviews for signs of compromise.

infosec.title: Hackers Use New ROMULUS ClickFix Platform to Deliver LegionLoader and Other Malware
infosec.summary: ROMULUS, a ClickFix delivery platform, was discovered using fake landing pages to make users run malicious commands. It was found to serve PowerShell staging scripts that deploy trojanized MSI installers or padded encrypted archives containing Legion Loader. Researchers found six IP addresses running the platform. One also hosted a ClickFix script linked to malicious ChatGPT Custom GPTs and Legion Loader, then retrieved further payloads.

infosec.title: Lambda Web Functions: Public by Default, and Already in Your lambda:* Grants
infosec.summary: Lambda Web Functions are a new AWS feature that allow for running a Node.js HTTP server behind a managed HTTPS domain. By default, the functions run with no authentication, and role credentials are included as environment variables, which could potentially be leaked for the full duration of the execution environment. Existing roles that grant lambda:* permissions have access to web functions by default, existing SCPs may not cover them, and visibility tooling may also miss functions, leading to the potential for shadow Web Functions being created and going unnoticed.

infosec.title: Package Manager Sandboxing
infosec.summary: Homebrew developer Andrew Nesbitt explains Homebrew 7.0's split fetch and install phases as well as the Landlock and Seatbelt-based sandboxes. Nesbitt then reviews the sandbox implementations, allowlist implementations, and sandbox proposals from other package managers. Some package managers like Go and Elm go a step further by fully removing code execution.

infosec.title: Inside Cairn: Open Windows into massive AI-Driven Cyber Operations
infosec.summary: NorForge found more than 20 publicly exposed Cairn panels used for malicious intrusion work. One Chinese-language cluster ran over 1,100 attack projects against e-commerce and payment systems in the US, Japan, Australia, and Canada, seeking unauthenticated RCE, file-upload webshells, SQL injection, and authentication bypasses. Another cluster targeted merchant payment, crypto, and pharmaceutical sites for card and cryptocurrency theft. The panels exposed targets, credentials, API keys, agent instructions, and successful compromises. Trufflehog found hundreds of secrets, with 11% verified valid. NorForge is notifying victims and seeking panel takedowns.

infosec.title: Address API and agentic AI risks
infosec.summary: Discover how excessive data exposure, tool poisoning, privilege escalation, and shifting trust boundaries affect modern architectures. Hear practical guidance for embedding security early, improving token hygiene, and preparing for regulatory scrutiny. Watch the webinar on demand.

infosec.title: Velociraptor Skills
infosec.summary: A collection of public, reusable Codex skills and DFIR tooling for Velociraptor setup, collection, hunting, and host analysis.

infosec.title: MIND (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: MIND is a data loss prevention platform that detects and blocks data exfiltration across email, endpoints, generative AI tools, and SaaS. It classifies content and context, then investigates events, tunes policies, and resolves issues.

infosec.title: Quicksand
infosec.summary: Quicksand is an async Python API for launching, controlling, and snapshotting QEMU virtual machines with a particular focus on sandboxing AI agents.

infosec.title: Our latest defenses against evolving web scams
infosec.summary: Chrome's Enhanced Protection added ClickFix detection that scrubs PII from copied commands, sends them to Safe Browsing for analysis, and warns users when the verdict comes back dangerous. Google also moved its Gemini scam detection from on-device to a server-side model that scores page intent and brand impersonation, and it added a lower-confidence "suspicious site" warning tier beneath the familiar red interstitial. The company claimed Enhanced Protection users were ten times safer than Standard Protection users, a figure drawn from Google's own measurement.

infosec.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
infosec.summary: A hacker used autonomous agents on the open-source Cairn platform to breach more than 100 sites, reportedly including John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. The attacker supplied intrusion tactics in under 100 Chinese characters. The breaches took about 23 hours. Norforge found over 20 likely malicious Cairn instances. John Deere said no sensitive data was accessed. SharkNinja contained the incident.

infosec.title: DHS to Ban DeepSeek From Federal Civilian Agencies
infosec.summary: The Department of Homeland Security announced a new ban on the procurement of products from DeepSeek. The directive cited national security concerns stemming from the potential for sensitive data to be stored or processed in China. Agencies will have 60 days to request exceptions to the policy.

infosec.title: All AI Attackers Need Is One Credential. We Found Over Half a Million.
infosec.summary: An AI agent broke into Hugging Face with one stolen credential. Truffle Security found 543,699 live credentials in the public code AI models train. Read what security leaders need to know before an agent finds theirs.

devops.title: Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust

The team is working with the TypeScript team to ensure the port remains compatible with the official language design. Rust allows the compiler to run in WebAssembly, which enables development environments to run in browsers or on embedded devices.

devops.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic

Content-addressed storage, server-side repository operations, and tiered caches reduced its source-control CPU and memory footprint 200× compared with its previous Git mirroring infrastructure.

devops.title: AI agents vs. Kubernetes: where each belongs in the control loop
devops.summary: Kubernetes operators suit deterministic reconciliation, while AI agents suit goals with unclear paths, according to a CNCF-sponsored piece. Use an observe, diagnose, propose, approve, reconcile, and verify loop, with autonomy phased from read-only investigation to approved low-risk changes.

devops.title: SIMD and Go

devops.title: vLLM
devops.summary: vLLM is a library for LLM inference and serving that originated in the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley. The open-source project now has over 2,000 contributors and supports more than 200 model architectures on Hugging Face.

Median review time fell from 4 minutes 9 seconds to 1 minute 32 seconds, while quality checks exposed trade-offs where cheaper configurations missed important findings.

design.title: Top Accessibility Errors in Production and How to Avoid Them

Automated scans catch only about 30 to 40 percent of issues, so keyboard and screen reader testing still has to happen before release.

The 70-20-10 learning model suggests that most professional development comes from practical experience and relationships, with formal education accounting for a relatively small portion. Structured courses can still be valuable when they address a specific knowledge gap, build confidence, or support a desired career direction rather than simply validating an already proven career.

design.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era
design.summary: Treating UI as a pure function of state lets developers see how a screen varies across roles, plans, billing statuses, and flags, which matters more now that agents take on front-end implementation work. In a worked example, an agent that tested only an owner account reported success on a delete action, yet viewers still saw the button despite a “View only” header. Rendering every state combination side by side exposes such gaps, so teams should make display-relevant state explicit and ask what an agent actually checked before merging.

marketing.title: PR for GEO: 4 Ways It Can Influence AI Visibility
marketing.summary: PR can improve AI visibility by earning citations for original research, reinforcing how third-party publications describe a brand, building backlinks, and increasing brand awareness. crypto.title: EIP-8288 Maximalism: Vitalik's Case Against New Ethereum Precompiles
crypto.summary: Precompiles and the EVM are the wrong venue for cryptography support in Ethereum because both require data to pass through the main chain as calldata, capping throughput at roughly 8 MB/s even with PeerDAS. Vitalik Buterin's proposed solution is EIP-8288 maximalism: compute heavy cryptography client-side, generate a STARK proof, and push only the proof through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism, so the chain records the result without seeing the underlying data or computation. This design lets developers use any signature scheme or cryptographic primitive without triggering new protocol-level precompile additions. Broader adoption would freeze Ethereum's precompile surface while keeping the base layer lean.

crypto.title: Faster, Aggregatable, and Quantum Safe Privacy Pools
crypto.summary: A new ethresear.ch proposal ports Tornado Cash-style privacy pools to Flock, a transparent hash-based SNARK using SHA-256 for the Merkle tree and nullifier derivation, removing the discrete-log assumptions in Pedersen commitments and Groth16. A stepwise circuit that runs one SHA-256 compression 34 times with a sumcheck glue argument cuts prover time 28x, from 810ms to 28.6ms at depth 32, with a 266 KiB proof size. An aggregation layer lets users prove withdrawals locally in ~19.5ms each, then folds N proofs into a single ~344 KiB proof that verifies in 46-64ms regardless of batch size. The scheme also includes a ZIP 2005-inspired quantum recovery protocol: if a cryptographically relevant quantum computer is announced, the pool freezes, and users withdraw through a post-quantum recovery verifier seeded from their original 256-bit key, leaving nullifier tracking intact.

it.title: The Autonomous Enterprise: What Happens When Work Runs Itself?

Industry experts emphasize that the best candidates for automation share three traits: they are reversible, bounded, and observable. Furthermore, enterprises must maintain human oversight where decisions carry material consequences while establishing clear operational boundaries and metrics that measure true process outcomes.

NVLink C2C moves up to 780 GB/s between sockets, but cross-socket core-to-core latency is around 660 ns. hardware.title: Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer
hardware.summary: This article presents views from Synopsys, Keysight, Renesas, Arteris, Cadence, and Mixel on how physical AI changes chip design. Engineers must handle unpredictable environments, safety and serviceability, and split designs between devices that can rely on the cloud and those that must run fully locally, such as vehicles. Several speakers frame it as a sensing and imaging problem as much as a compute one.

hardware.title: AI hardware design is the easy part, the lossy physical interface is the bottleneck
hardware.summary: AI will soon be superhuman at hardware design, but the digital-to-physical interface is lossy. Building real parts means navigating CNC/CAM translation, tolerance stacking, vendors, and scale, while measuring reality is sparse, slow, expensive, and sometimes qualitative. Demand is expected to shift toward suppliers of machined parts, harnesses, and components, plus better simulation and process-knowledge data.
